newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Western Metals Pillara zinc mine to proceed.
newsitem.headline: Western Metals Pillara zinc mine to proceed.

text.p: Western Metals Ltd said on Friday that it had given final approval for the development of the Pillara zinc and lead mine in Western Australia's Kimberley region at a total cost of more than A$100 million.
The company said work on the Pillara mine and plant, which had previously been known as Blendevale, would begin immediately with commissioning expected within 11 months.

The underground mine, located in the Lennard Shelf area and 50 km northwest of its existing Cadjebut operations, has reserves of 10.6 million tonnes grading 8.1 percent zinc and 2.5 percent lead which would be mined and processed through a new plant designed to treat 1.5 million tonnes of ore annually.
Pillara had a minimum mine life of eight years.
Funding for the Pillara mine will be from cashflow and loans which will ultimately see the company gear up to just under 20 percent, Western Metals said.
"When in full production, Western Metals' Lennard Shelf operations will become one of the largest underground mining complexes in Australia," the company said.

The region would rank as the seventh largest zinc mining complex in the world when Pillara reached full production with estimated annual production of 170,000 tonnes of zinc and 65,000 tonnes of lead contained in concentrates.

Concentrates from the Pillara mine would be trucked 260 km to the port of Derby where Western Metals said it was spending about A$10 million on a new export facility that could handle up to 400,000 tonnes of concentrate annually, it said.
Full production from the Cadjebut operations for the 1996/7 year ended June 30 was 66,362 tonnes of zinc and 19,680 tonnes of lead contained in concentrates, Western Metals said.
For 1997/98, output from the Cadjebut mill will continue at around 900,000 tonnes a year with the bulk of ore coming from Goongewa mine which will be fully commissioned in September, it said.
The original Cadjebut mine and the new Kapok mine will continue to produce the balance of the Cadjebut mill feed requirements, it said.
At June 30, the Lennard Shelf had resources totalling 26 million tonnes grading 8.0 percent zinc and 3.6 percent lead or more than 10 years mine life at the expanded rate, Western Metals said.

Although current reserves are only 13.8 million tonnes grading 8.2 percent zinc and 3.3 percent lead, mined tonnes have exceeded initial reserve estimates at both Cadjebut and Goongewa by about 100 percent.
Western Metals said it is mounting an aggressive exploration programme which has already identified a number of targets which could see the existing four mines in the Lennard Shelf increase further.
Western Metals sells concentrates to smelters in South Korea, Thailand, India, Japan and the United States.
